newsitem.title: UK: NatWest Markets faces revamp - FT.
newsitem.headline: NatWest Markets faces revamp - FT.

text.p: National Westminister Bank Plc is considering reshaping NatWest Markets, its investment banking arm, in response to pressure from institutional investors critical of the bank's performance, the Financial Times said on Wednesday.

Directors of NatWest Markets who are reviewing its future are likely to recommend to the bank's board later this month that it is scaled down by moving its corporate lending and treasury operations into the commercial bank.

The proposals, which are backed by Derek Wanless, NatWest chief executive, would reverse the original blueprint for NatWest Markets when it was formed in 1992 as a joint corporate and investment banking operation.

However, it would also make it easier for it to sell NatWest Markets as a stand-alone entity because it will have disentangled its lending relationships with big companies from those of the investment bank, the Financial Times said.

The review is unlikely to lead to the closure of any of the main UK operations. Directors expect about 100 of its 8,000 staff to lose their jobs, with these cuts largely occurring in overseas operations.
NatWest has been under pressure from investors as a result of its loss of 77 million stg ($130 million) due to unauthorised option trading in March.
This eventually led to the resignation of Martin Owen, chief executive of NatWest markets, in June.
